name: js-nav-thin-sample
description: Ledgerly (clean-site) rebuilt the way a large corporate site looks to a non-JavaScript fetcher: the navigation is rendered by a script, so the served HTML links only to a sign-up page and three legal pages; robots.txt points at a sitemap index whose first child lists feature and integration URLs that match no page role, while the child that lists about-us, contact-us and the newsroom is never read. The sampler therefore reaches the home page alone and records every role as missing. The home page itself is fine: it has a heading, a call to action, testimonials, dates, JSON-LD and a search form, but no address, no FAQ and no press link. Pins the absence gate: what this sample cannot see must not be reported as absent from the site.

expected.notes: The four gated ids all fail at probe level, and each was a false positive on a real corporate site before the gate: 'no address' when the contact page was never fetched, 'key facts missing' when the pages that state them were never fetched, 'no FAQ' likewise, and 'no newsroom' from a two-page sample of a site whose newsroom sits behind a script-rendered menu. After compose each is not_evaluated (role_page_not_sampled, or navigation_not_readable for the press check), produces no finding, and is explained in limitations. en.cta.missing is not gated because it is a claim about the home page that was read, and it passes here because the header button is in the first viewport. The sitemap index is the adobe.com shape: 91 children of which the sampler reads the first.
